# `bots` — 10. Quality

*Which quality scenarios must hold, and which constants decide when something is stale, retried,
paused or given up?*

## Built: timing

The constants that decide when a bot waits, retries, pauses or halts. The table is **generated** from
the constants by `python3 scripts/render_bots_design_tables.py --write`, which reads each value from
the code; `tests/unit/scripts/test_render_bots_design_tables.py` fails when it differs from a fresh
render. Do not edit it by hand.

<!-- generated by scripts/render_bots_design_tables.py: timing -->
| What | Value | Where |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Price is stale after; grace at start | 60 s; 60 s | `src/modules/bots/domain/grid/price_freshness.py` → `PRICE_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`, `PRICE_START_GRACE_SECONDS` |
| A reference price older than this is refused | 10 s | `src/modules/bots/domain/grid/reference_price.py` → `REFERENCE_PRICE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` |
| A halted feed counts as back only with a tick younger than | 15 s | `src/modules/bots/domain/grid/price_freshness.py` → `RECOVERY_TICK_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` |
| Every bot's feed is checked every | 5 s | `src/modules/bots/application/services/watches/bot_price_watch.py` → `CHECK_EVERY_SECONDS` |
| Account-level loss cap: the bots are sampled every; it trips when it cannot judge for; the price a bot saves to its file is at most this old | 15 s; 120 s; 30 s | `src/modules/bots/application/services/loss_cap/account_loss_cap.py` → `SAMPLE_EVERY_SECONDS` · `src/modules/bots/domain/loss_cap/loss_cap_policy.py` → `UNJUDGED_TRIP_AFTER` · `src/modules/bots/application/kinds/grid/watch/grid_price_reaction.py` → `MARK_PRICE_SAVE_SECONDS` |
| Order pacer default caps: open orders, spacing, orders per minute | 100; 250 ms; 60 | `src/modules/trading/contracts/owner_budget.py` → `DEFAULT_OWNER_BUDGET_CAPS` |
| Order pacer: the window it keeps beyond trading's rate window, for the moment trading's stamp trails the pacer's turn | 2 s | `src/modules/bots/adapters/monotonic_order_pacer.py` → `STAMP_JITTER` |
| Most bots not at rest one venue holds at once | 5 | `src/modules/bots/domain/venue_bot_cap.py` → `MAX_ACTIVE_BOTS_PER_VENUE` |
| User stream down for this long halts; reconciled every; checked every | 120 s; 300 s; 15 s | `src/modules/bots/application/services/watches/user_stream_watch.py` → `UserStreamLimits.down_limit`, `UserStreamLimits.reconcile_every`, `UserStreamLimits.check_every` |
| Sleep: heartbeat; a gap over this is a sleep; fresh-price attempts and spacing | 15 s; 60 s; 4 × 15 s | `src/modules/bots/application/services/watches/sleep_watch.py` → `SleepLimits.check_every`, `SleepLimits.gap_over`, `SleepLimits.price_attempts`, `SleepLimits.price_retry_every` |
| Wait before each automatic retry of a stop | 10, 30, 60, 120, 300 s | `src/modules/bots/application/kinds/grid/stop/grid_stop_retry.py` → `STOP_RETRY_DELAYS` |

| The request gate closes at this share of the minute's weight; a One-way position mode is kept | 70 % of 6000 on Spot, of 2400 on Futures; 60 s | `src/modules/trading/adapters/binance/exchange_call_policy.py` → `SOFT_WEIGHT_RATIO`, `SPOT_WEIGHT_LIMIT` · `src/modules/trading/adapters/binance/venue_sessions.py` → `FUTURES_WEIGHT_LIMIT` · `src/modules/trading/adapters/binance/position_mode_memory.py` → `TTL_SECONDS` |

## Built: halt recovery

*Which halts recover by themselves, with what dwell and how often?* The table is the **effective**
policy of every kind on every market, **generated** from the code like the one above: the common layer
(`bots/domain/halt_recovery_policy.py` → `COMMON_LAYER`), the kind's (`bots/domain/grid/grid_kind.py` →
`GRID_RECOVERY_LAYER`) and the venue's (`bots/contracts/venue_profile.py` → `VenueProfile`, field
`recovery_layer`) folded in that order, later winning ([the decision](../../../Tasks/epics/EPIC-042_halt_auto_recovery/DECISION_2026-10-17_halt_auto_recovery.md)
§2.3). The figures are the owner's: dwell 120 s, three attempts per rolling 24 h counted per bot, and
an alert after 15 min of waiting. A halt uses it from `EPIC-042C`: the Grid's quiet feed and down stream wait here and recover by themselves. The exchange's pause joined them in `EPIC-042F`, with a dwell of the 2 s margin; a Futures venue clears the lower layers and lists that one reason only.

<!-- generated by scripts/render_bots_design_tables.py: halt-recovery -->
| Kind | Market | Reason | Dwell | Attempts per window | Stalled after | Decided by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `grid` | Spot | `price_feed_stale` | 120 s | 3 per 24 h | 900 s | `common` layer |
| `grid` | Spot | `rate_limited` | 2 s | 3 per 24 h | 900 s | `grid` layer |
| `grid` | Spot | `user_stream_down` | 120 s | 3 per 24 h | 900 s | `common` layer |
| `grid` | Futures | `rate_limited` | 2 s | 3 per 24 h | 900 s | `futures` layer |
<!-- end generated: halt-recovery -->

## Built: what must hold, and what proves it

| Scenario | Held by |
| :--- | :--- |
| A bot's state changes only through its lifecycle table; an undeclared change is refused | `bots/domain/bot_lifecycle_fsm_matrix.py` → `next_target`, `InvalidBotTransitionError` |
| A fill already counted is never counted twice | `.../grid_facts.py` → `GridFacts._apply_fill` (`EPIC-035P`) |
| A bot is never reported `STOPPED` while an order carrying its tag rests | `.../grid_stop_sequence.py` → `GridStopSequence.run` |
| A restart places nothing; a running bot waits in `RECOVERING` for an open order session | `.../bot_restore_service.py` → `BotRestoreService.restore_all` |
| A second copy of the app changes no bot | `bots/module.py` → `BotsModule.boot` (`EPIC-035H`) |
| A quiet price feed halts a bot that holds or lays orders | `bots/domain/bot_lifecycle_fsm_matrix.py` → `PRICE_STALENESS_HALTS` (`EPIC-035A`) |
